summary: Iteration 48: Validated 'Menú Flotante' (QuickMenu) end-to-end. Backend: 8/8 pytest cases passed - public GET seeds + returns 4 default items active+ordered (no _id leak), admin GET requires auth (401 without token), admin POST/PUT/DELETE full CRUD with persistence verification, inactive items hidden from public, 404 on missing id, 400 on empty update. Frontend: Floating menu (data-testid=quick-menu) visible on left at y=354px desktop, 4 cyan icons (rgb(0,231,255)) inside dark navy (#33404f) rounded-r block, hover via real mouse.move triggers slide-in label 'SeniorClub' with opacity 1. Admin: tab-quick-menu testid present and clickable, table renders 4 rows with Orden/Ícono/Nombre/URL/Estado/Acciones columns, 'Nuevo Ítem' opens quick-menu-modal with all required fields (Nombre, URL, Ícono Lucide, Ícono personalizado URL, Orden, Activo). Toggle button (toggle-{id}) flips active state and persists to backend (verified active=False then active=True via API after each click). All 9 existing admin tabs (pending, all, plans, blog, podcast, leads, convenios, reviews, crear-residencia) still have correct data-testids - no regression.

critical_code_review_comments: quick_menu_routes.py is clean: uses item_id (uuid) for public identifier, projects out _id everywhere, async motor calls, Pydantic schemas, admin guard via get_current_user+require_admin. Good.

QuickMenu.jsx is small and focused (~75 lines). Uses Link for internal URLs and <a target=_blank> for external (https://) URLs - correct behavior. Could be enhanced with aria-label on each icon link for accessibility.
AdminPanel.jsx now ~2300+ lines and continues to grow as new tabs are added; consider splitting per-tab content/modals into separate components (Phase2 refactor).
Seed defaults run on every public GET (count_documents then insert) - cheap but adds 1 extra mongo call per request. Could move to startup hook.
